findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, `exec` evaluates it with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` passed the value as one argument without shell interpretation. Retain argument-based execution to prevent command injection and preserve process ownership behavior.

findings.title: [P2] Avoid shell interpretation so cancellation still owns the Git process
findings.body:
On POSIX, a valid branch name such as `HEAD&sleep${IFS}60` makes `exec` launch a shell command tree rather than one Git process. Killing the returned `ChildProcess` signals only the shell, allowing spawned/background descendants to survive and making exit events no longer represent completion of the intended `git show`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve argument-based execution to prevent shell command injection
findings.body:
`branch` is interpolated into a shell command. Any caller supplying input such as `main; rm -rf <path>` can execute arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile` call passed the branch directly to Git without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command. Any caller-controlled value such as `main; rm -rf ...` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges; the previous `execFile` argument array prevented shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
